items.followUp: State the two conditions required for a body to be in equilibrium.

rubric.why: The first condition is translational equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the resultant force is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the net/resultant force on the body must be zero.

rubric.why: The second condition is rotational equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the resultant torque (moment) is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the net/resultant torque or moment must be zero.

modelAnswer: The resultant force acting on a body must be zero (first condition of equilibrium).
The resultant torque acting on a body must be zero (second condition of equilibrium).

items.followUp: Why is magnetic force described as a non-contact force?

rubric.why: A non-contact force acts without the objects touching.
rubric.description: States that gravitational force acts without physical contact.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the bodies do not have to touch.

rubric.why: Gravity acts through a gravitational field between masses.
rubric.description: Identifies the gravitational field or attraction between masses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the gravitational field or gravitational attraction between masses.

modelAnswer: Gravitational force acts between masses without physical contact; the bodies do not have to touch.
It acts through the gravitational field around a mass, so it is a non-contact force.

items.followUp: Define work and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: This is the textbook definition of energy.
rubric.description: Defines energy as the capacity or ability to do work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition.

rubric.why: The SI unit of energy is the joule.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating joule (J).

modelAnswer: Energy is the capacity to do work.
Its SI unit is the joule (J).

items.followUp: A body of mass 2 kg moves with a velocity of 5 m s⁻¹. Find its kinetic energy.

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is calculated using the correct formula.
rubric.description: Writes the kinetic-energy formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for KE = ½mv².

rubric.why: The values are substituted and the kinetic energy is evaluated with its unit.
rubric.description: Finds the kinetic energy as 100 J.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution and answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 0.5 kg, v = 20 m s⁻¹.
Formula: K.E. = ½mv².
Substitution: K.E. = ½ × 0.5 kg × (20 m s⁻¹)².
Answer: K.E. = 100 J.

items.followUp: State and derive Newton’s second law of motion for a body of constant mass.

accept: change in momentum per unit time
rubric.why: This states Newton’s second law in terms of momentum.
rubric.description: States that force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the law in terms of rate of change of momentum.

accept: F proportional to change in momentum/time
rubric.why: The proportional relationship is expressed mathematically.
rubric.description: Writes the force–momentum relationship.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the proportionality or its equation.

rubric.why: In SI units, the proportionality constant is one.
rubric.description: Uses the SI proportionality constant to obtain the force equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the constant is one in SI units or giving F = Δp/Δt.

rubric.why: Substituting p = mv for constant mass gives F = ma.
rubric.description: Derives the acceleration form of the law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for deriving F = m(v − u)/t and hence F = ma.

modelAnswer: Newton’s second law states that the force acting on a body is directly proportional to the rate of change of its momentum, and acts in the direction of that change.
F ∝ change in momentum/time.
F = k(Δp/Δt); in SI units, k = 1, so F = Δp/Δt.
For a body of constant mass, p = mv; therefore F = m(v − u)/t = ma.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and derive the expression K.E. = ½mv².

accept: capacity to do work due to position
rubric.why: This defines potential energy by the position of the body.
rubric.description: Defines potential energy as energy possessed due to position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition.

rubric.why: The force required to lift the body equals its weight.
rubric.description: Identifies the lifting force as the body’s weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for F = mg.

rubric.why: Work done in lifting is force multiplied by vertical displacement.
rubric.description: Relates work done to force and height.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for W = Fs, with s represented by the height h.

rubric.why: Substituting F = mg and s = h gives the required result.
rubric.description: Derives the expression for gravitational potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining P.E. = mgh.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position.
To raise a body of mass m through a height h, the upward force required is equal to its weight: F = mg.
Work done against gravity = force × displacement = Fh.
Therefore, P.E. = W = mgh.

items.followUp: How does increasing the number of significant figures affect the precision of a measured quantity?

rubric.why: Precision is indicated by the significant figures in the measurement.
rubric.description: Relates precision to the number of significant figures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the number of significant figures indicates precision.

rubric.why: More significant figures indicate a more precise measurement.
rubric.description: States the direction of the relationship.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that a greater number of significant figures means greater precision.

modelAnswer: The precision of a measured quantity is indicated by its number of significant figures.
The greater the number of significant figures, the greater the precision.

items.followUp: What is meant by uniform acceleration?

rubric.why: Uniform speed involves equal distances travelled.
rubric.description: Mentions equal distances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that equal distances are covered.

rubric.why: The equal distances must be covered in equal time intervals.
rubric.description: Mentions equal time intervals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying that the distances are covered in equal intervals of time.

modelAnswer: Uniform speed is the speed of a body that covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
